data.other_hard: Jewish (patrilineality acknowledged); professionally recognized doctoral candidate; admission to doctoral studies at a state or state-recognized university in Germany, or in an EU member state or Switzerland if German citizen, or at a non-European university in justified cases; non-German citizens pursuing doctorate in Germany must reside in Germany for funding duration; last degree completed no more than five years before application; German language skills at level B2; excludes medicine
data.evidence_sentence: We support professionally recognized Jewish doctoral candidates in all subject areas and all disciplines (except medicine).
data.notes: Non-Jewish doctoral candidates can apply only for research projects in Germany dealing with Jewish topics (this is a separate route). Special circumstances and periods of childcare or care for relatives are considered in selection, not as requirements. Funding is three years standard plus possible six-month extension. Deadline not stated on page; rolling is inferred from the text saying applications should be submitted in the initial phase of dissertation writing, not a fixed date. Funding type not specified.
